from manim import *
import numpy as np

# === TeachingScene Base Class ===
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

# === Section 2 Scene ===
class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Waves", lines)
        
        # Constants for positioning
        WAVE_TL = "B1"
        WAVE_BR = "E6"
        WAVE_SCALE = 0.35 # Calculated to fit 2 cycles in the right side area
        
        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # Helper to create a sine wave path
        def create_sine_path(phase, amp, color=WHITE):
            # Using 4*PI for two full cycles
            return FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: amp * np.sin(x - phase),
                x_range=[0, 4 * np.pi],
                color=color
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create base wave object
        wave = create_sine_path(0, 1.0, WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
        
        # Updater for smooth oscillation
        def wave_updater(m):
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            a = amp_tracker.get_value()
            c = m.get_color()
            # Generate new path data based on current trackers
            new_path = create_sine_path(p, a, c)
            self.place_in_area(new_path, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
            m.set_points(new_path.get_points())
        
        wave.add_updater(wave_updater)
        self.add(wave)
        
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Dots that track peak and trough
        peak_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA)
        
        def tracker_dots_updater(group):
            p_dot, t_dot = group
            points = wave.get_points()
            if len(points) > 0:
                # Find the current highest and lowest visible points on the wave path
                peak_idx = np.argmax(points[:, 1])
                trough_idx = np.argmin(points[:, 1])
                p_dot.move_to(points[peak_idx])
                t_dot.move_to(points[trough_idx])
        
        dots_group = VGroup(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        dots_group.add_updater(tracker_dots_updater)
        self.add(dots_group)
        
        # Flash the dots to highlight phase points
        self.play(
            Flash(peak_dot, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(trough_dot, color="#FF00FF", flash_radius=0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Continue oscillation to show dots following the wave movement
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(dots_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Introduce a second wave to represent overlap/interference
        wave2 = create_sine_path(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value(), WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave2, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
        wave2.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        
        def wave2_updater(m):
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            a = amp_tracker.get_value()
            c = m.get_color()
            new_path = create_sine_path(p, a, c)
            self.place_in_area(new_path, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
            m.set_points(new_path.get_points())
            
        wave2.add_updater(wave2_updater)
        self.add(wave2)
        
        # Animate constructive interference by merging into a single Cyan wave with double amplitude
        self.play(
            wave.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            wave2.animate.set_color("#00FFFF").set_stroke(opacity=1),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0),
            phase_tracker.animate.increment_value(PI),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Remove the duplicate wave mobject after they have visually merged
        self.remove(wave2)
        
        # Final result oscillation of the combined wave
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.increment_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)
